Modern.brandNameRationale: Named for the kicktail — the upward bend at the back of a deck, introduced by Larry Stevenson at Makaha in 1969 and codified through the early 1970s. The kicktail is what turned a flat plank into a maneuverable skateboard; everything from the ollie to the modern street trick depends on it. We name the brand after the geometry that made the sport possible.
Modern.industrySummary: Hardgoods skate brands fall into two camps: heritage labels that lean on 1970s LA mythology, or aggressive graphics-led street brands. There is a clean middle for a modern hardgoods company that talks about deck shape — concave, wheelbase, tail kick — the way a road-bike brand talks about geometry.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Polar Skate Co. (polarskateco.com) holds the considered modern slot. Isle Skateboards (isleskateboards.com) is the art-led modern peer. Welcome Skateboards (welcomeskateboards.net) sets the shape-forward precedent. We sit closer to Isle, sharper on engineered geometry.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern hardgoods brand for riders who care about the shape of the deck.

targetAudience.primary: 18 to 35. Skates three days a week. Owns two setups. Reads Closer and Free Skate Mag. Can tell a 14-inch wheelbase from a 14.5 by feel.
behaviors: Buys decks by shape spec, not graphic
Sets up trucks by axle width and bushing duro
Watches full parts the day they drop

dos: Name the concave, the tail steepness, the wheelbase
Print the shape number on the topsheet
Speak to the rider, not the spectator
donts: Photograph decks on a white pedestal

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark. Kicktail Supply set in a tight modern grotesk, with the K's lower leg extended into an upward kick that mirrors a tail profile. The kick alone is the favicon.

colorPalette.name: Maple
colorPalette.meaning: Canadian hard-rock maple, the standard deck material.

colorPalette.name: Hazard Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Construction cone, the color of the street.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for shape specs and wheelbase
typography.rationale: The mono carries the deck specs. The regular carries the brand.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Named for the empty backyard pools of 1976 drought-era Los Angeles, when the Z-Boys turned drained kidney pools into the first vertical skate terrain. Mahaka evokes the era of named pools (the Dog Bowl, the Canyon, the Soul Bowl) without trading on any active mark. Treats the pool as the brand's club.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury in skate has been an oxymoron — the closest the market gets is heritage reissue lines and limited deck drops. There is room for a premium brand that takes the pool-skating era as its reference and treats the deck like a piece of equipment, not merch.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Hopps (hoppsbrand.com) sits in the considered-craft niche. Antihero Skateboards (antiheroskateboards.com) holds the pool-skate heritage slot. Lowcard Mag (lowcardmag.com) is the cultural peer. We sit above all three, in a premium one-drop-per-season position.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A premium pool-skating house — heavyweight decks, brass hardware, members-only drops.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Skated through the 90s. Owns a 9-inch pool deck. Has skated a real backyard pool. Buys one deck a year and rides it until it cracks.

dos: Name the pool, the coping, the year
Speak in the language of the bowl

Luxury.logoDirection: A serifed wordmark. Mahaka Pool Club set in a 1970s-era condensed serif, with a pool-shape (kidney) silhouette as the hallmark. Foiled in brass on the topsheet.

colorPalette.name: Coping Tile
colorPalette.meaning: Original blue pool tile around the coping.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for deck numbers and pool index
typography.rationale: Canela gives the brand a heritage stance. The mono carries the catalog data.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Named for the deck's concave — the lateral curvature, measured in millimeters from edge to center, which is the single most-discussed spec among skaters. A one-word brand pointing at the shape, not the graphic.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most skate brands compete on graphic. A minimal hardgoods brand that competes on concave depth and deck shape has space — the customer is the rider who buys blanks and pro models for the wood, not the print.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Polar Skate Co. (polarskateco.com) is the design-minimal peer. Isle Skateboards (isleskateboards.com) holds the considered-minimal slot. Magenta Skateboards (magentaskateboards.com) is the European-minimal precedent. We sit below all three on visual noise, pure shape.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimal hardgoods brand built around deck shape and nothing else.

targetAudience.primary: 22 to 40. Skates every weekend. Buys blanks or low-graphic pro decks. Knows the difference between medium and steep concave.
behaviors: Sets up new decks the day they arrive
Sands down graphics they don't like

dos: Print the concave depth on every deck
Say nothing the spec sheet doesn't say
donts: Add a tagline to the topsheet

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark. CONCAVE set in a tight modern grotesk, with a single curved line beneath it that mirrors a deck's cross-section. The curve alone is the favicon.

colorPalette.name: Ply Cream
colorPalette.meaning: Raw maple ply, sanded but unstained.

typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for concave depth and mold numbers
typography.rationale: One typeface family. The mono carries the spec, the regular carries the brand.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Named for the Pacific Coast skate corridor — Venice, Huntington, Encinitas, Oceanside — the geographic backbone of US skateboarding. The Co. suffix and place-name framing position the brand as wholesale-ready, suitable for skate schools, municipal park programs, and B2B distribution.
Corporate.industrySummary: The skate hardgoods market has very few B2B-friendly umbrella brands suited to municipal skatepark contracts, skate school supply, and wholesale distribution. Most heritage brands are too rider-specific. There is room for a corporate-feeling umbrella that supplies decks, trucks, and wheels at scale.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: NHS Distribution (nhs-inc.com) is the wholesale parent peer. Dwindle Distribution (dwindledist.com) holds the multi-brand supplier slot. Skate One (skateone.com) sets the OEM precedent. We sit alongside Dwindle, with a coastal regional identity.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A wholesale-ready hardgoods house supplying decks and components to the skate corridor.

targetAudience.primary: Skate shop buyers, municipal parks-and-rec procurement, skate school operators. Buys by the case, not the deck.
behaviors: Orders by SKU and lead time

dos: Quote lead times and case quantities

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a shield. Pacific Coast Skate Co. set in a clean American sans-serif, paired with a simple shield containing a stylized wave-and-deck silhouette. The shield works on shipping cartons.

typography.primary: Aktiv Grotesk for the wordmark and document headers
typography.secondary: Aktiv Grotesk for body and price lists
typography.rationale: One typeface family. Reads professional on a purchase order and clean on a shipping box.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Named for the slappy — the act of grinding a curb without ollieing onto it, the original street trick that predates the ollie's adoption on street. Curb culture is the heart of street skating before parks, and Slappy Curb Press positions the brand as a zine-and-deck creative imprint rooted in that lineage.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative skate imprints are crowded with art-collab and graphic-led brands, but most lean on illustration rather than the actual street objects skaters interact with. There is room for a zine-and-deck imprint that takes a single street feature — the curb — as its whole identity.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Bronze 56k (bronze56k.com) is the creative imprint peer. Quartersnacks (quartersnacks.com) holds the NYC street-culture slot. Hockey Skateboards (hockeyskateboards.com) is the art-led creative precedent. We sit alongside Bronze, sharper on curb obsession.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative skate imprint built around curb culture — decks, zines, hand-screened graphics.

targetAudience.primary: 20 to 35. Skates the same three curbs every week. Owns every Bronze 56k tape. Buys decks for the graphic and the zine that comes with them.
behaviors: Wax the curb before skating it

dos: Name the curb, the spot, the city
Pair every deck drop with a zine

Creative.logoDirection: A hand-drawn wordmark. Slappy Curb Press lettered in a chunky brush script, sitting on a horizontal line that suggests a curb edge. The curb-line alone is the favicon.

colorPalette.name: Wax Yellow
colorPalette.meaning: Skate wax rubbed into the curb edge.

typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for zine body copy and deck specs
typography.rationale: The hand-lettering carries the imprint voice. The mono carries the structural information.
